lines: Arpeggiator that plays the pitches arriving on one polyphonic cable in a chosen order, one note per clock
Chooses the order the input pitches are played in: Straight-R, Straight-L, Straight-RL, Straight-LR, Crab-R, Crab-L, Crab-RL or Crab-LR, and the chosen name is shown on the display
Sets how many steps into the arpeggio playing starts, 0 to 10, wrapped round to the length of the arpeggio
A voltage here chooses the order the pitches are played in, in place of the ARPEGGIO knob; whole volts from 0V to 7V pick the eight orders
A positive voltage holds the arpeggio as it is and blocks changes to the order, while randomisation triggers are accepted; a negative voltage blocks randomisation as well
A trigger swaps two notes of the running arpeggio with each other, either of which may already have been played
A polyphonic gate cable choosing which channels of the V/OCT input are played: only channels at a positive voltage are used, and with nothing patched here every channel is used
The polyphonic cable of 1V/octave pitches the arpeggio is built from, read afresh at the start of each pass; with nothing patched a single 0V pitch is used
A rising edge moves the arpeggio on to its next note, and the module plays nothing until something is patched here
The 1V/octave pitch of the note being played, clamped to -10V to 10V
Carries 10V on each note of the arpeggio, as a 1ms trigger, a retrigger or a continuous gate according to the menu
A 1ms trigger on the clock edge that follows the last note of the arpeggio
Menu — Gate Mode chooses what the GATE output carries: a 1ms trigger on each note, a retrigger that drops low for 1ms between notes, or a gate held high while the arpeggio runs
Menu — Play last note in cyclical arpeggios sets whether the Straight-RL and Straight-LR orders sound the note at the turn twice or omit the repeat
Arpeggiator that builds a pattern of intervals around one root pitch, one note per clock
Chooses the shape of the pattern: Diverge, Converge, Return, Bounce, Rez or On The Run, and the chosen name is shown on the display
Sets how many steps the pattern runs for, 1 to 16
Sets the size of each step, -24 to 24; a positive value raises the pitch step by step and a negative value lowers it
Chooses what one step means: a semitone, a step of the major scale or a step of the minor scale
Sets how many steps into the pattern playing starts, 0 to 10
A voltage here chooses the shape of the pattern, in place of the PATT knob; whole volts from 0V to 5V pick the six shapes
A voltage here sets how many steps the pattern runs for, in place of the LEN knob; whole volts from 1V to 16V
A voltage here sets the size of each step, in place of the STEPS knob; whole volts from -24V to 24V
A positive voltage holds the pattern as it is and blocks changes to it, while randomisation triggers are accepted; a negative voltage blocks randomisation as well
A trigger swaps two notes of the running pattern with each other, either of which may already have been played
The 1V/octave root pitch the pattern is measured from, read at the start of each pass; with nothing patched 0V is used
A rising edge moves the pattern on to its next note, and the module plays nothing until something is patched here
The 1V/octave pitch of the note being played, clamped to -10V to 10V
Carries 10V on each note of the pattern, as a 1ms trigger, a retrigger or a continuous gate according to the menu
A 1ms trigger on the clock edge that follows the last note of the pattern
Menu — Gate Mode chooses what the GATE output carries: a 1ms trigger on each note, a retrigger that drops low for 1ms between notes, or a gate held high while the pattern runs
Menu — Play last note in cyclical patterns sets whether the note at the turn of a Return pattern is sounded twice or the repeat is omitted
Shift-register chord looper: a loop of 2 to 16 chords, clocked round, whose head is replaced by a fresh chord at a set chance
Sets the chance that the chord reaching the head of the loop is kept as it was; fully clockwise the loop is frozen and the lamp shows red, and turning it down raises the chance of a new chord
A voltage above zero freezes the loop so that no chord is replaced, whatever the X knob is set to
Sets how far a replacement chord may stray from the rule in force: at its lowest the chords keep to the chosen key and stay plain, and raising it brings in outside roots and harsher chords
Adds to the Y knob, 10V covering the whole of the knob's range, and the sum is clamped to that range
Sets the key the chords are drawn from, C to B
A voltage here sets the key, in place of the ROOT knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve keys, or read as a 1V/octave pitch if the menu says so
Sets the mode the chords are drawn from, Ionian through Locrian
A voltage here sets the mode, in place of the MODE knob; 0V to 10V spread across the seven modes
Sets how many chords are held in the loop, 2 to 16
A rising edge shifts the loop on by one place and the chord at the head is sent to the pitch outputs
The lowest note of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch, and the same jack carries all six notes as a polyphonic cable
One note of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch; a chord of three or four notes fills the remaining outputs by repeating its own notes from the root up, in the octave the menu chooses
Menu — Chord Selection picks the rule a replacement chord follows: Random draws from the C major scale, Simple draws triads from the chosen key and mode, Galaxy follows the Galaxy module's rule
Menu — Repeat Notes chooses the octave of the notes repeated to fill six outputs from a three- or four-note chord: an octave lower, the same octave, an octave higher, or a random octave
Menu — Allowed Chord Inversions limits which inversions may be picked at random: root position only, root and first, or root, first and second
Menu — Root Volt Scaling chooses how the ROOT input is read, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve keys spread across 0V to 10V
Circle of fifths: turns a key and a mode into the control voltages that drive the chord sequencers and quantisers, and steps round the circle on triggers
A trigger moves the position one place anticlockwise round the circle and the ROOT output follows; a trigger arriving here and at ROT R at once returns to the key the ROOT knob sets
A trigger moves the position one place clockwise round the circle and the ROOT output follows; a trigger arriving here and at ROT L at once returns to the key the ROOT knob sets
Sets the key the circle starts from, C to B, shown in red on the circle
A voltage here sets the starting key, in place of the ROOT knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve keys, or read as a 1V/octave pitch if the menu says so
Sets the mode, Ionian through Locrian
A voltage here sets the mode, in place of the MODE knob; 0V to 10V spread across the seven modes
The current key as a voltage for the root input of Progress, Bombe, Galaxy or Scale Quantizer
The current mode as a voltage, 0V to 10V across the seven modes, for the mode input of Progress, Bombe or Galaxy
Menu — Input Volt Scaling chooses how the ROOT input is read, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve keys spread across 0V to 10V
Menu — Output Volt Scaling chooses how the ROOT output is written, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve keys spread across 0V to 10V
Six oscillators, one per voice, each with its own wave, octave, detune, level and pan, mixed to a stereo pair
The 1V/octave pitch for the first voice, and the polyphonic source for any voice whose own pitch jack is empty, one channel per voice
The 1V/octave pitch for that voice, replacing the channel it would otherwise take from the first pitch jack
Chooses the wave for that voice: sine, saw, double saw, square or even
Shifts that voice by whole octaves, -3 to 3
Detunes that voice by up to one semitone either way
The modulation voltage for that voice's pulse width, attenuated by its own PWM CV knob before it reaches the width
Sets the pulse width of that voice's square wave, -1 to 1
Attenuates the voltage at that voice's pulse width modulation input, 0 to 100%, before it is added to the width knob
Sets the level of that voice in the mix, 0 to 100%
Places that voice between the left and right sides of the mix
Attenuates every pan setting towards the centre: at 100% each voice is panned as its own PAN knob says, and at 0% all six are centred
The left side of the stereo mix, carrying every voice as its pan places it, despite the wiki giving this jack the odd voices; with nothing patched into RIGHT it carries the mono sum
The right side of the stereo mix, carrying every voice as its pan places it, despite the wiki giving this jack the even voices; with nothing patched into LEFT it carries the mono sum
Chord.notes: The wiki says the odd-numbered voices go to LEFT and the even-numbered ones to RIGHT when both outputs are patched; the installed code pans every voice across both sides and sends the mono sum to whichever single output is patched.

lines: Semi-random chord generator: each trigger moves the choice around a galaxy whose arms are chord qualities and whose stars are root notes
A trigger picks the next chord and sends it to the pitch outputs
Sets the key the chords are drawn from, C to B
A voltage here sets the key, in place of the ROOT knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve keys, or read as a 1V/octave pitch if the menu says so
Sets the mode the chords are drawn from, Ionian through Locrian
A voltage here sets the mode, in place of the MODE knob; 0V to 10V spread across the seven modes
Raises the chance that the chord comes from outside the chosen key or mode, 0 to 100%; the lamp flashes green for a chord from the key underlying the mode and red for one taken at random
The lowest note of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch, and the same jack carries all six notes as a polyphonic cable
One note of the current chord as a 1V/octave pitch; a chord of three or four notes fills the remaining outputs by repeating its own notes from the root up, in the octave the menu chooses
Menu — Chord Selection picks how the next chord is found: Random moves as much as two arms and two scale steps, in Key keeps the root in the chosen key, in Mode draws root and quality from the mode
Menu — Repeat Notes chooses the octave of the notes repeated to fill six outputs from a three- or four-note chord: an octave lower, the same octave, an octave higher, or a random octave
Menu — Allowed Chord Inversions limits which inversions may be picked at random: root position only, root and first, or root, first and second
Menu — Root Volt Scaling chooses how the ROOT input is read, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve keys spread across 0V to 10V
Toolkit for generative patches: an LFO crossed with pink noise, a clock filtered by chance into delayed gates, and a slewed sample of the mix
Sets the frequency of the LFO in octaves, -8 to 10, where 0 gives 1Hz and 10 gives 1024Hz
Sweeps the LFO wave without stepping, from sine through triangle, saw and square and back to sine
Attenuates the voltage at the FM input, 0 to 100%, before it is added to the LFO frequency in octaves
Crossfades the LFO against the voltage at the AM input, 0% leaving the LFO alone and 100% passing only the AM input
Crossfades the modulated LFO against the internal pink noise, 0% giving the LFO alone and 100% giving noise alone, and the result leaves by the MIXED output
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, -2 to 6 in octaves, from 15 to 3840 beats per minute
Sets the chance that a clock tick is accepted and goes on to make a gate, 0 to 100%
Sets the delay between an accepted tick and the start of the gate, 0 to 1 second
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off the delay, up to 2 seconds either way, drawn from a bell curve and never taking the delay below zero
Sets the length of the gate, from 1ms to 1 second
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off the gate length, up to 2 seconds either way, with 1ms as the shortest gate made
Sets the shape of the slew towards each new sample, linear fully anticlockwise and exponential fully clockwise
Sets how slowly the output moves towards each new sample, 0 to 100%, from an instant jump to a long glide
Attenuates the modulated LFO, 0 to 100%, before it reaches the LFO output and before it is mixed with the noise, despite the panel drawing it in the row that ends at OUT
A voltage here is added to the WAVE knob on the same scale, sweeping the LFO wave
The modulation voltage for the LFO frequency, attenuated by the FM CV knob and then added in octaves
The voltage crossfaded against the LFO by the AM CV knob; with nothing patched here the LFO passes unchanged
A voltage here is added to the NOISE MIX knob, 1V covering the whole of the knob's range, and the sum is clamped to that range
A rising edge here takes the place of the internal clock and offers a tick to the probability stage
A voltage here is added to the CLOCK knob in octaves of tempo, and the sum is clamped to the knob's range
A voltage here is added to the PROB knob, 10V covering the whole range, and the sum is clamped to that range
A voltage above zero stops the output moving, holding it at the voltage it has reached
The modulated and attenuated LFO, without the noise mixed in
The LFO and the noise mixed as the NOISE MIX knob sets, and this is the signal that gets sampled
The internal pink noise on its own, -10V to 10V
The sampled voltage after slewing and attenuation; the menu can quantise it to semitones
A 10V gate for each accepted clock tick, after its delay and for its own length; the lamp shows red while the delay runs and green while the gate is open
Menu — Quantise rounds the OUT voltage to the nearest semitone on a 1V/octave scale, or leaves it as sampled
Menu — CV Offset sets the range of the noise and of the LFO, either -5V to 5V or 0V to 10V
Note — a tick arriving before the delay and the gate have finished is discarded, so a clock faster than the delay plus the gate is thinned out
Generative.notes: The wiki calls the trigger input SAMPLE; the panel prints TRIGGER. The panel draws ATTN in the row that ends at OUT, but in the installed code the level it sets is applied to the LFO before the noise mix, so it scales the LFO and MIXED outputs and the voltage that gets sampled, not the OUT jack after sampling.

lines: Turns each clock tick into sixteen polyphonic gates, each with its own random delay and length, after dividing the clock and filtering it by chance
The clock; each rising edge is counted, and the module makes nothing until something is patched here
Sets the chance that a tick surviving the division goes on to make gates, 0 to 100%
Sets the delay between the tick and the start of the gate, 0 to 1 second
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off the delay, up to 2 seconds either way, drawn from a bell curve and never taking the delay below zero
Sets the length of the gate, from 1ms to 1 second
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off the gate length, up to 2 seconds either way, with 1ms as the shortest gate made
Divides the incoming clock, 1 to 64, so that only every nth tick goes on to the probability stage
Sixteen channels of 10V gates from one accepted tick, each channel given its own delay and length; a tick arriving before a channel's gate has finished is discarded for that channel
Menu — Randomize first output sets whether channel 1 gets its own random delay and length like the rest, or the plain values set by the DELAY LEN and GATE LEN knobs
Four channels that turn triggers into gates with a random delay and a random length, and divide the trigger count
The trigger for that channel; with nothing patched, the channel takes the trigger from the nearest channel above that has one, and only while this channel's output is patched
Sets the delay between the trigger and the start of that channel's gate, 0 to 1 second, on a logarithmic sweep that is finest at the short end
A voltage here sets that channel's delay in place of its knob: 0V gives no delay, 1V gives 1 second and 3V gives 2 seconds
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off that channel's delay, up to 2 seconds either way, drawn from a bell curve and never taking the delay below zero
A voltage here sets that channel's delay spread in place of its knob, on the same scale as the delay, so 1V gives 1 second of spread
Sets the length of that channel's gate, from 1ms to 1 second, on a logarithmic sweep that is finest at the short end
A voltage here sets that channel's gate length in place of its knob: 1V gives 1 second and 3V gives 2 seconds
Sets how much random time is added to or taken off that channel's gate length, up to 2 seconds either way, with a positive minimum so that every trigger makes a gate
A voltage here sets that channel's gate spread in place of its knob, so 1V gives 1 second of spread
Divides that channel's trigger count, 1 to 64, so that only every nth trigger makes a gate
The 10V gate for that channel, delayed and lengthened as that channel's knobs set; the lamp shows red while the delay runs and green while the gate is open
Note — the tempo of the trigger arriving at each input is shown beside it in beats per minute
Eight-step chord sequencer keyed to a scale, holding 32 parts, sending the chord of the current step out as one polyphonic cable
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, -2 to 6 in octaves, from 15 to 3840 beats per minute
A voltage here is added to the CLOCK knob, one octave of tempo per volt
Starts and stops the sequence, one press each way, and the lamp is lit while it runs
A rising edge advances the sequence by one step and takes the place of the internal clock
Sets the sequence back to step 1
A trigger sets the sequence back to step 1
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before repeating, 1 to 8
A voltage here is added to the STEPS knob at one step per volt, and the sum is clamped to 1 to 8
Sets the key the chords are drawn from, C to B
A voltage here sets the key, in place of the ROOT knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve keys, or read as a 1V/octave pitch if the menu says so
Sets the mode the chords are drawn from, Ionian through Locrian
A voltage here sets the mode, in place of the MODE knob; 0V to 10V spread across the seven modes
Chooses which of the 32 stored parts is played and edited, 0 to 31
A voltage here chooses the part, in place of the PART knob; 0V to 10V spread across the 32 parts
Chooses which stored part the COPY button copies from, 0 to 31
Copies the part chosen by SOURCE into the part now selected, overwriting what was there
A voltage here selects the step directly and the clock is ignored: the voltage is rounded to a whole number and wrapped round the number of steps in use
Switches that step's gate on and off; its lamp is red while the gate is on, green while the sequence reaches that step with the gate on, and dim yellow while it reaches the step with the gate off
That step's own gate, at 10V while the sequence is on the step and its gate is switched on
10V while the sequence is on any step whose gate is switched on
The chord of the current step as six polyphonic channels of 1V/octave pitch
Menu — Chord Selection limits what the step editor offers: All Chords, only chords belonging to the mode, or chords coerced into the mode
Menu — Gate Mode chooses what the gate outputs carry: a trigger at each step, a retrigger that drops low briefly, or a gate held for the whole step
Menu — Repeat Notes chooses the octave of the notes repeated to fill six channels from a three- or four-note chord: an octave lower, the same octave, an octave higher, or a random octave
Menu — Root Volt Scaling chooses how the ROOT input is read, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve keys spread across 0V to 10V
Note — the root, chord, inversion and octave of each step are set from drop-down lists on the display, not from knobs
Trigger sequencer built from sixteen clock dividers in a four by four grid, with the triggers of each row and each column summed to one output
Sets the division for that cell, 0 to 64; at 0 the cell is switched off and never fires
Sets the chance that the cell fires when its division comes round, 0 to 100%
Moves that cell's triggers earlier or later against the master clock, -64 to 64 beats
Switches that column's output on and off, one press each way, and the lamp is lit while the output is passing triggers
Switches that row's output on and off, one press each way, and the lamp is lit while the output is passing triggers
A rising edge advances the beat count that every divider is measured against
A trigger sets the beat count back to zero
A polyphonic cable added to the division knobs at 6.4 divisions per volt; channel 1 reaches the top left cell and the channels run left to right, then down a row
A polyphonic cable added to the probability knobs, 10V covering the whole range; channel 1 reaches the top left cell and the channels run left to right, then down a row
A polyphonic cable added to the shift knobs at 12.8 beats per volt; channel 1 reaches the top left cell and the channels run left to right, then down a row
A 1ms trigger whenever any cell in that column fires
A 1ms trigger whenever any cell in that row fires
Ruckus.notes: Parameters 52 to 63 are declared but never configured or placed on the panel, so they have no line and no tag.

lines: Eight independent quantisers sharing one key and one scale, each with its own hold, octave shift and change trigger
The 1V/octave pitch into that quantiser; a polyphonic cable is quantised channel by channel
A rising edge here samples that quantiser's input and holds the quantised pitch until the next edge; with nothing patched the pitch follows the input without being held
Shifts that quantiser's output by whole octaves, -3 to 3, after quantisation
The quantised 1V/octave pitch for that quantiser, with its octave shift and the global transposition added
A 1ms trigger each time that quantiser's output pitch changes
Sets the root note of the scale, C to B, despite the maker's tooltip on it describing the TRANS knob's transposition
A voltage here sets the root note, in place of the KEY knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve notes, or read as a 1V/octave pitch if the menu says so
Chooses the scale: chromatic, the seven modes, major and minor pentatonic, harmonic minor or blues
A voltage here chooses the scale, in place of the SCALE knob; 0V to 10V spread across the twelve scales
Transposes every output by whole semitones, -11 to 11, after quantisation and outside the chosen scale
Adds to the TRANS knob at one semitone per volt, transposing every output after quantisation
Menu — Root Volt Scaling chooses how the KEY input is read, as a 1V/octave pitch or as the twelve notes spread across 0V to 10V
ScaleQuantizer2.notes: The maker's tooltip on the KEY knob carries the description 'Transposition of all outputs post-quantisation'; the installed code assigns that text to KEY_PARAM while it belongs to the TRANS knob, and KEY sets the root note of the scale.

lines: Noise source sampled on a trigger, with the output slewing towards each new sample
A rising edge takes a new sample of the noise, despite the panel printing HOLD; the output then slews towards it and stays there until the next edge
Sets how slowly the output moves towards each new sample, 0 to 100%, from an instant jump to a long glide
Sets the shape of the slew, linear fully anticlockwise and exponential fully clockwise
Chooses the colour of the noise: white fully anticlockwise, pink at the centre, brown fully clockwise
Attenuates the slewed output, 0 to 100%
The sampled voltage after slewing and attenuation
The raw noise on its own, -10V to 10V
SLN.notes: The wiki names the input SAMPLE and gives the knobs as IN, SL, CL and AT; the panel prints HOLD over the input jack, and the input is a rising-edge trigger that takes a fresh sample.

lines: Splits one polyphonic cable into sixteen mono outputs, and merges sixteen mono inputs into one polyphonic cable
The polyphonic cable to be split; its first channel goes to the first MONO OUT jack, its second to the second, and so on
One channel of the cable patched into CV IN, at 0V when the cable does not reach that channel
One channel of the polyphonic CV OUT cable; the output carries as many channels as the highest numbered MONO IN jack in use
Sets the voltage the GATE output carries on channels whose MONO IN jack is patched, -10V to 10V
A voltage here sets what the GATE output carries on those channels, in place of the BIAS knob
The merged polyphonic cable, carrying as many channels as the highest numbered MONO IN jack in use, with 0V on channels whose own jack is empty
A polyphonic cable with as many channels as CV OUT, carrying the BIAS voltage on channels whose MONO IN jack is patched and 0V on the rest
Displays the per-channel voltages of two polyphonic cables side by side, along with a chosen operation on the pair
One of the two polyphonic cables read: its channel count and the voltage on each of its channels are listed on the display
The chosen operation applied channel by channel to the two inputs, with as many channels as the wider of the two
Menu — Operation chooses what this module calculates and sends out: A plus B, A minus B, or A plus B rounded to the nearest semitone, which the display names as a note with its octave and cents
Oscilloscope that draws every channel of one polyphonic cable as its own coloured trace
The polyphonic cable drawn; each channel gets its own trace and colour
Scales the traces vertically in powers of two, -2 to 2, so 0 draws them at size and 1 draws them twice as tall
Spaces the traces apart vertically, 0 to 3, with all sixteen drawn on top of each other at 0
Moves every trace up or down the display, -16 to 16
Sets the span of time drawn across the display, halving with each step from about 8 seconds to about 8ms
Menu — Colour Schemes picks the set of sixteen trace colours: Classic, Constant V, Constant L, Full Circle, Synthwave or User
Menu — Load colour scheme reads a JSON file of colours from disk and uses it as the User scheme
Note — clicking the blank strip below and between the SPREAD and SHIFT knobs makes the traces sweep apart and back on their own, with the SPREAD knob ignored; clicking there again stops it
Two polyphonic tools on one panel: one that cuts a cable down to a set number of channels, and one that deals a cable out into two
The polyphonic cable to be cut down
Sets how many channels the MASK section passes, 1 to 16; channels above that are dropped
The input cable cut down to the number of channels the CHAN knob sets
The polyphonic cable to be dealt out into two
Sets the block size the channels are dealt out in: 0 sends all to OUT1, 1 alternates channel by channel, 2 deals in pairs, 3 in fours, 4 sends the first eight to OUT1 and the rest to OUT2
The channels dealt to the first side, packed down so they start at channel 1
The channels dealt to the second side, packed down so they start at channel 1
Sets the voltage on each channel of a polyphonic cable by hand, with optional quantising to semitones
Sets the voltage on that channel of the output, -10V to 10V
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16; channels above that are sent 0V
The polyphonic cable carrying the voltage set for each channel
Menu — Quantise rounds every channel voltage to the nearest semitone on a 1V/octave scale, or passes it as the knob sets it
Arpeggiator over as many as six input pitches, repeating and transposing the arpeggio to make a longer sequence
One of the pitches the arpeggio is played over, as a 1V/octave voltage; jacks with nothing patched are skipped, and with all six empty a single 0V pitch is used
A rising edge moves the sequence on by one note
A rising edge starts the sequence from its beginning; with nothing patched here the sequence runs on the clock without being started
Starts the sequence from its beginning, once for each press
Holds the pitches, the arpeggio and the pattern at the values of the running cycle, randomised notes included, until it is pressed again; when it is off the pitches are read afresh each cycle
Chooses the order the input pitches are played in: Right, Left, RightLeft or LeftRight
A voltage here chooses the order the pitches are played in, in place of the ARP knob; whole volts from 0V to 3V
Chooses how the arpeggio is transposed from one repetition to the next: Up, Down, UpDown, DownUp, Rez or On The Run
A voltage here chooses the transposition pattern, in place of the PATTERN knob; whole volts from 0V to 5V
Sets how far each repetition is transposed from the one before, -24 to 24 steps, and at 0 the arpeggio repeats at the same pitch
A voltage here sets the transposition per repetition, in place of the STEPS knob; whole volts from -24V to 24V
Sets how many times the arpeggio repeats in one sequence, 1 to 16
A voltage here sets how many repetitions the sequence runs, in place of the LENGTH knob; whole volts from 1V to 16V
Chooses what one transposition step means: a semitone, a step of the major scale or a step of the minor scale
The 1V/octave pitch of the note being played
Carries 10V on each note of the sequence, as a 1ms trigger, a retrigger or a continuous gate according to the menu
A 1ms trigger at the last note of each repetition of the arpeggio
A 1ms trigger at the last note of the whole sequence
Menu — Gate Mode chooses what the GATE output carries: a 1ms trigger on each note, a retrigger that drops low for 1ms between notes, or a gate held high while the sequence runs
Note — this module is kept for old patches and Arp 3.1 and Arp 3.2 take its place between them
Eight-step chord sequencer: each step sets a root, a chord and an inversion, and the six notes come out on jacks of their own
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, -2 to 6 in octaves, from 15 to 3840 beats per minute
A voltage here is added to the CLOCK knob, one octave of tempo per volt
Starts and stops the sequence, one press each way, and the lamp is lit while it runs
A rising edge advances the sequence by one step and takes the place of the internal clock
Sets the sequence back to step 1
A trigger sets the sequence back to step 1
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before repeating, 1 to 8
A voltage here is added to the STEPS knob at one step per volt, and the sum is clamped to 1 to 8
The key of the sequence, 0V to 10V across the twelve keys; patching this and MODE at the same time turns the step knobs from naming root notes to naming scale degrees
The mode of the sequence, 0V to 10V across the seven modes; patching this and ROOT at the same time turns the step knobs from naming root notes to naming scale degrees
Sets the root note of that step's chord, or the degree of the scale for that step when ROOT and MODE are both patched
Chooses the chord for that step from the table of 98, or from the chords the scale degree allows when ROOT and MODE are both patched
Chooses the inversion of that step's chord: root position, first or second
Switches that step's gate on and off; its lamp is red while the gate is on, green while the sequence reaches that step with the gate on, and dim yellow while it reaches the step with the gate off
One note of the current step's chord as a 1V/octave pitch; a chord of fewer than six notes fills the remaining jacks by repeating its own notes from the tonic up
That step's own gate, at 10V while the sequence is on the step and its gate is switched on
10V while the sequence is on any step whose gate is switched on
Menu — Gate Mode chooses what the gate outputs carry: a trigger at each step, a retrigger that drops low briefly, or a gate held for the whole step, which is how the module starts
Note — this module is kept for old patches and Progress MkII takes its place
Quantiser that snaps one pitch to a scale and reports which interval of that scale the note landed on
The 1V/octave pitch to be quantised
Sets the root note of the scale, 0V to 10V across the twelve notes; with nothing patched the root is C
Chooses the scale, 0V to 10V across chromatic, the seven modes, major and minor pentatonic, harmonic minor and blues; with nothing patched the scale is chromatic
The quantised 1V/octave pitch
Goes to 10V for one sample each time the quantised pitch changes
Carries 10V while the quantised note stands that many semitones above the root of the scale, and 0V at every other moment
